correctness.rationale: The unscaled base-3/2 digit-parity word satisfies aligned triples (x_{3m},x_{3m+1},x_{3m+2})=(x_{2m},1-x_{2m},x_{2m}). For y_m=x_{2m}, y_{3m}=y_{3m+1} rules out four alternating y symbols. Ten alternating x letters would give three consecutive crossing edges y_m→y_{m+1}, contradiction; length-nine x[12:21]=101010101 witnesses sharpness. Every length-3p factor periodic with gcd(p,3)=1 has at least p-1 complete aligned triples whose starts run over all except possibly one residue modulo p; the two alternating edges from each cover every cyclic edge, forcing p even and the factor alternating. Since 3p≤9, p=2; period1 excluded by lack of constant triples. Hence 6≤L≤9 and maximum coprime-period exponent 9/2, while period-three fifth power occurs at x[18:33]=(101)^5. Verified 10,000 symbols independently from direct digit extraction, cube searches for candidate periods up to 50 coprime to 3 and both sharp witnesses. Infinite theorem rests on block/cyclic cover proof, not a finite prefix.
